comparison: Both evaluations support the structural characterization of photoreceptor degeneration (C3, C40-C49). OpenEval emphasizes multiple complementary methods and temporal progression. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the 'rapid cell death' phenotype and call it 'rigorous.' OpenEval R1 also covers apoptosis markers (C50-C55) which peer reviewers address separately in R2.

OpenEval R1 includes apoptosis characterization (C50-C55) as part of broader degeneration documentation. Peer R2 specifically highlights apoptosis findings as a manuscript strength, with Reviewer 1 stating 'They showed that rapid cell death is through apoptosis.' Both fully support these claims.

OpenEval R1 includes GLS2 characterization and light-independence control (C36-C39, C43). Peer R6 specifically notes consideration of GLS2 as a confounding factor 'added strength to this work.' Both evaluations support the isoform specificity and experimental controls.

Perfect claim overlap (C56-C63) on synaptic and inner retinal changes. Both evaluations support the ultrastructural and immunofluorescence findings. OpenEval emphasizes temporal sequence supporting secondary degeneration. Peer reviewers note the consideration of synaptic connectivity 'added strength' to the work.

Perfect claim overlap (C64-C67) on functional deficits measured by ERG. Both evaluations fully support the findings. OpenEval emphasizes correlation with structural changes. Peer Reviewer 3 specifically notes 'Histology and ERG were carefully done' as a strength.

Strong overlap on inducible knockout findings (C70-C75). Both evaluations support the evidence that GLS is required for maintenance of mature photoreceptors. OpenEval includes additional claims about cone knockout (C77-C78). Peer reviewers call the two cre-line approach 'rigorous' and accept the similar phenotypes as a strength.

Perfect claim overlap (C82-C83) on nucleotide biosynthesis findings. Both evaluations support the metabolomics data and conclusion that GLS is not critical for nucleotide synthesis. Peer Reviewer 3 notes 'Necessary metabolomic study was performed and appreciated.'

Perfect claim overlap (C84-C92) on redox changes. Both evaluations support the multiple complementary measurements of oxidative stress and glutathione changes. OpenEval notes appropriately modest interpretation. Peer reviewers accept redox findings as part of overall metabolic characterization showing glutamine is critical for 'redox balance.'

Perfect claim overlap (C94-C104) on metabolic characterization including stable isotope tracing. Both evaluations support the comprehensive metabolomics approach. OpenEval emphasizes the inference that glucose oxidation is not increased. Peer Reviewer 3 states 'Necessary metabolomic study was performed and appreciated.'

Partial overlap on stable isotope tracing (C105, C109). OpenEval R8 also covers α-KG rescue (C111-C112) which peer reviewers address in R12. Both support the tracing data demonstrating reduced glutamine flux through TCA cycle. Peer reviewers accept this as part of necessary metabolomic characterization.

Overlap on α-ketoglutarate rescue experiment (C111-C112). Both evaluations support the modest rescue effect and interpretation that TCA cycle support is not the primary mechanism. Peer Reviewer 3 notes 'Some rescue experiments were performed, and revealed possible mechanism' as a strength.

Partial overlap on amino acid depletion (C114-C116). OpenEval R9 focuses on ISR activation and rescue. Peer R11 emphasizes amino acid findings as part of overall metabolic characterization. Both support the metabolomics data. Peer reviewers call the data 'convincing' for showing glutamine is critical for 'biomass.'

Partial overlap on ISR activation markers (C117-C118). OpenEval R9 includes full ISR characterization and ISRIB rescue. Peer R13 focuses on ISR as part of innovative asparagine/ISR linkage. Both support ISR activation findings. Peer Reviewer 2 calls findings 'intriguing and innovative.'

Overlap on ISRIB rescue experiment (C119-C121). Both evaluations support the evidence that ISR activation contributes to degeneration. OpenEval emphasizes temporal and mechanistic relationships. Peer reviewers accept ISRIB rescue as demonstrating ISR involvement and call it 'innovative.'

Strong overlap on asparagine rescue (C131-C132, C178). Both evaluations strongly support this novel finding. OpenEval notes the claim of first evidence appears justified. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly highlights asparagine supplementation findings as 'intriguing and innovative.' Peer Reviewer 3 notes rescue experiments 'revealed possible mechanism.'

Overlap on overarching conclusions (C190-C191). Both evaluations support the main mechanistic conclusions linking amino acid depletion, ISR activation, and cell death. OpenEval emphasizes integration of multiple evidence lines. Peer reviewers call it 'fundamental' and 'convincing' with Reviewer 3 noting it is 'Interesting and novel.'

Minimal overlap (C4 only). OpenEval R11 focuses on integrating mechanistic pathway evidence. Peer R11 emphasizes amino acid depletion findings (C114-C116, C146-C150) as part of metabolic characterization. Both support the overall metabolic findings showing glutamine is critical for multiple cellular functions.

Partial overlap on discussion/interpretation claims (C133-C139, C143-C144). OpenEval R12 focuses on comparison to other metabolic knockouts and importance of glutamine catabolism. Peer R18 covers extensive discussion claims. Peer Reviewer 2 notes authors 'were careful not to overstate their claims' and provide 'solid conclusions.'

Minimal overlap (C145 only). OpenEval R12 uses IND-cKO data to support conclusions about glutamine catabolism importance. Peer R4 focuses on the inducible knockout as demonstrating requirement in mature photoreceptors. Both accept this as strengthening the main conclusions.

Minimal overlap on discussion claims (C77-C78). OpenEval R4 includes speculation about cone knockout and synaptic transmission as part of inducible knockout results. Peer R18 covers these as discussion/interpretation. Both accept the interpretations as appropriately cautious.

Peer R17 covers extensive introductory/background claims (C1-C2, C8-C35) supported by prior literature. These foundational claims are not explicitly evaluated as separate results by OpenEval, though they provide context for the experimental findings. Peer reviewers accept the background without challenge.
